description: NASA verilerini tarımsal karar destek süreçlerine dönüştürmek amacıyla bir araya gelmiş bir yazılım mühendisliği ekibiyiz. Python, veri işleme, makine öğrenmesi ve yazılım mimarisi yetkinliklerimizi birleştirerek Field Shift temasına yönelik uygulanabilir ve sağlam bir prototip geliştirmeye odaklanıyoruz. summary:
GeoKernel is a data-driven agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers adapt to the changing conditions caused by climate change. Traditional farming decisions based on past experience are becoming less reliable as temperature, precipitation, and soil moisture patterns continue to shift.

Our platform uses NASA POWER data to analyze temperature, precipitation, and soil moisture conditions for a selected agricultural location. GeoKernel transforms these environmental datasets into meaningful insights by assessing climate and production risks and supporting decisions related to suitable planting periods and crop strategies. Users can explore analyses for their own fields and create agricultural plans that better reflect current environmental conditions.

GeoKernel is important because it transforms global Earth science data into local, practical agricultural decisions. Our goal is to help farmers adapt to climate change, use natural resources more consciously, and contribute to a more sustainable and climate-resilient agricultural future.
details:
What GeoKernel Does and How It Works

GeoKernel is a climate-adaptive agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers make more informed, data-driven decisions based on local environmental conditions.

Climate change is altering environmental factors such as temperature, precipitation, and soil moisture, making traditional agricultural decisions based solely on past experience increasingly unreliable. GeoKernel addresses this challenge by transforming global Earth science data into practical, field-level insights.

Users define their agricultural fields using location information. GeoKernel then uses NASA POWER data to analyze environmental conditions for the selected location, including temperature, precipitation, and soil moisture. These datasets are transformed into a decision-support process that helps assess climate and production risks, monitor environmental conditions, identify suitable planting periods, and compare agricultural strategies. Users can review these insights and develop agricultural plans that better reflect the environmental conditions of their own fields.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The main goal of GeoKernel is to help farmers adapt their decisions to changing climate conditions by supporting them with location-specific environmental data rather than relying exclusively on traditional practices.

The platform aims to:

  • Help farmers better understand changing environmental conditions,
  • Evaluate temperature, precipitation, and soil moisture at the field level,
  • Support more informed decisions regarding climate and production risks,
  • Provide decision support for planting periods and agricultural strategies,
  • Encourage more conscious use of water and other natural resources,
  • Contribute to more sustainable and climate-resilient agricultural practices.

The intended long-term impact of GeoKernel is to bridge the gap between global Earth science data and practical local decisions. Helping individual farmers make better decisions for their own fields can contribute to broader agricultural communities that are better prepared to adapt to climate change and use natural resources more efficiently.

Technologies and Tools Used

GeoKernel was developed using modern web development and data analysis technologies. The backend was developed with Python and FastAPI to handle data processing and analytical services. NASA POWER data is accessed through an API and integrated into the environmental analysis process.

The frontend was developed using React and JavaScript to provide an interactive interface where users can explore their agricultural fields, environmental analyses, and agricultural strategies. Python-based data processing tools are used to process and analyze environmental datasets. API-based data access, database management, analytical processing, and user interaction were combined to create a functional end-to-end prototype.

Creativity and Innovation

The innovative aspect of GeoKernel lies in transforming NASA's global Earth science data into field-level decision support rather than simply displaying environmental information.

Our approach follows this transformation:

Global Earth Data → Local Environmental Analysis → Field-Level Insights → Agricultural Decision Support

Instead of only showing users what environmental data is available, GeoKernel aims to help them understand what that data means for agricultural decisions. This creates a connection between complex scientific datasets and practical actions that can be considered at the farm and field level.

Factors We Considered

While developing GeoKernel, we considered several important factors:

  • The fact that climate change affects regions and agricultural areas differently,
  • The need to translate global environmental data into local insights,
  • The importance of making complex scientific data understandable for users,
  • The effects of temperature, precipitation, and soil moisture on agricultural decisions,
  • The importance of location-specific analysis,
  • The need for an accessible and user-friendly interface,
  • The meaningful integration of NASA data as a core component of the decision-making process,
  • The potential to scale the platform for different regions and agricultural scenarios.

In conclusion, GeoKernel is a data-driven and user-friendly decision-support platform that adapts NASA Earth science data to local agricultural conditions. Our project aims to reduce the gap between global environmental information and everyday agricultural decisions while supporting a more sustainable and climate-resilient future for farming.
